reviewer: Teoh Kai Hong (blanket chat approval 2026-11-06; not an itemized review)
method: Windows hardening/risk.py rubric: R = 6I + 5E + 4P + 3L + 2D; I/P from consequence/privilege categories, L from Server level and Automated/Manual, E from surface baseline, D from compatible history.

session_hygiene.reason: Session management weakness unrelated to passwords: minor reduction in security posture (4.14a score 2 tier).

remote_shell.reason: Remote interactive administrative service (OpenSSH): significant network/remote exposure on the shared scale, the same semantic tier as the Windows remote-desktop surface baseline, derived from SSH facts only.

local_exploit_mitigation.reason: Kernel/userspace exploit mitigation or confinement that matters after an attacker already runs code locally: limited local exposure.

system_software.reason: Installed package versions across all services; reachability depends on which services listen, so controlled network/remote exposure without asserting Internet reachability.

privilege_escalation_path.reason: Weakens a barrier between unprivileged code and root: may contribute to administrative access (same tier as the Windows 4.14c score 4 wording).

host_network_path.reason: Governs host packet handling rather than accounts or rights: limited privilege implications (4.14c score 2 tier).

2.4.1.2.rationale: Group- or world-accessible /etc/crontab discloses system jobs; write access would let an unprivileged user run commands as root.

1.3.1.1.rationale: Without the AppArmor packages, mandatory access control cannot confine compromised programs.

1.5.1.rationale: Predictable memory layout makes memory-corruption exploits easier to write.

1.5.3.rationale: Core dumps of privileged programs can disclose sensitive memory contents.

1.5.4.rationale: Prelinking modifies binaries, interfering with integrity checking and easing shared-library tampering.

2.1.2.rationale: An unneeded unauthenticated discovery service adds network attack surface and discloses host information.

5.3.3.2.2.rationale: Short passwords are practical to guess or crack.

5.4.1.1.rationale: Passwords without a maximum age extend the useful life of a stolen credential.

5.4.1.3.rationale: Too little expiry warning leads to rushed, weaker password choices or lockouts.

5.4.1.5.rationale: Accounts with expired passwords stay usable indefinitely instead of being disabled.

5.2.2.rationale: Without a pseudo-terminal, a program run through sudo can keep access to the user's terminal after it exits.

5.2.3.rationale: Privileged command use is harder to review without a dedicated sudo log.

3.3.1.rationale: A host that forwards packets can act as a router and bypass network segmentation.

3.3.2.rationale: Sending ICMP redirects can be abused to alter other hosts' routing.

3.3.8.rationale: Accepting source-routed packets lets senders dictate paths around network controls.

4.1.3.rationale: An inactive host firewall exposes every listening service.

4.1.4.rationale: Missing loopback rules allow spoofed loopback traffic from the network or break local services.

4.1.7.rationale: Permissive default policies admit traffic that no rule explicitly allows.

6.3.1.1.rationale: Without the audit packages, security-relevant events cannot be recorded.

6.3.1.2.rationale: A stopped audit service records no events.

6.3.1.3.rationale: Processes started before the audit daemon are not audited unless auditing is enabled at boot.

6.3.3.4.rationale: Unaudited time changes can hide activity by confusing log timelines.

6.3.3.8.rationale: Changes to user and group identity files go unrecorded.

6.3.3.6.rationale: Use of privileged programs by ordinary users goes unrecorded.

5.1.20.rationale: Direct root login over SSH exposes the root identity and removes individual accountability.

5.1.19.rationale: Accounts with empty passwords could log in remotely without any secret.

5.1.16.rationale: More authentication attempts per connection make online guessing easier.

5.1.7.rationale: Unresponsive sessions are not detected and remain open.

5.1.10.rationale: Host-based trust lets one compromised host authenticate users to another.

5.1.21.rationale: User-supplied environment variables can subvert access restrictions or programs at login.
